idiom_name: interface delegation (`by`) with the audited methods overridden
implementation_notes: Kotlin generates the whole forwarding surface for you: class AuditedPayments(private val inner: Payments) : Payments by inner compiles to methods that delegate to inner, and only the audited methods need an override carrying the audit logic - the hand-written Decorator/Interceptor skeleton is replaced by compiler-generated delegation plus one override. Where a framework already provides the seam, use it instead (Ktor application plugins/interceptors around a pipeline, Spring AOP), because Kotlin itself has no annotation-driven interception. Note that members overridden in this way are not visible to the delegate object's own implementations, so auditing cannot be pushed into the delegate.
pitfalls: Delegated members do not see the overrides: the delegate's own implementations call their own methods (documented Kotlin behaviour), so a call made inside inner is never audited by the delegating class.
A blocking audit sink inside a suspend override stalls the dispatcher coroutine; hand events to a non-blocking channel or a dedicated dispatcher.
Interface delegation does not intercept calls that hold the delegate itself, so the wrapper must be the only instance callers receive.
